designs.title: R1 · Local pressure-film cells
designs.status_detail: Tooling, wiring and code are supplied. No physical R1 performance has been established.
designs.summary: Add six thin resistive contact cells to the existing finger: two on the hard nail and four on the compliant TPU.
designs.signal: Local electrical conductance; local force estimates require calibration.
designs.best_for: A first contact-coverage and material experiment with common materials.
designs.tradeoff: Handmade laminates, drift, hysteresis, wear and bending behavior need measurement.

Two N0 pressure-film laminates: 0.10 mm conductive film between copper electrodes and insulating backing
One on the object-facing surface of each hard nail prong
CH2–CH5
Four separate pressure-film cells on conformal silicone saddles
Along the four TPU contact regions, ordered from tip to base
Readout
Pico + two ADS1115 boards; six resistor dividers and reference checks
At the wrist/base; sensing-cell leads run along the finger
designs.placement: Use the R1 CH0–CH5 cut patterns. The two nail pads use the thin N0 construction first; it adds about 0.40 mm nominal mounted thickness. Keep the central nail notch open.

designs.title: L1 · Whole-finger root force
designs.status_detail: Purchased-cell fixtures, aluminum-carrier CAD and readout code are supplied. Physical fit and force/moment behavior remain untested.
designs.summary: Place a purchased load cell in the complete finger load path while retaining the original contact surfaces.
designs.signal: Aggregate normal force after calibration; it does not provide a contact-location map.
designs.best_for: A separate force benchmark covering normal loads on both nail and TPU.
designs.tradeoff: Adds 20 mm reach and 18.46 mm root width in the CAD. Housing fit, moments, gravity and cable forces remain important.
sensors: Force cell
One TAL220B 5 kg load cell; selected reference SparkFun SEN-14729
Between the fixed jaw carrier and floating finger carrier
Readout
NAU7802, INA219 supply/current monitoring, level shifter and Pico
At the fixed side or wrist
designs.placement: The original finger attaches to the floating carrier. The cell's two solid ends connect separately to the fixed and floating sides. No cable, screw or housing contact may create a parallel load path.

visual.alt: L1 original finger with fixed and floating carriers and a purchased load-cell reference

next_steps: Test the cell in its independent fixture.

designs.title: B1 · Magnetic bending insert
designs.status_detail: Insert/spine CAD, checked sensor PCB files and raw readout code are supplied. No physical force calibration or 20 N qualification is supplied.
designs.summary: Keep the TPU compliant, put four magnets inside it, and read their motion using five fixed magnetic heads. Add two thin nail pads for precision-task contact coverage.
designs.signal: Magnetic-field/deformation observations plus optional nail conductance; calibrated force is not yet available.
designs.best_for: The current magnetic pilot on the existing thin ENPIRE finger.
designs.tradeoff: Adds 3.65 mm global width before screw heads, or 6.05 mm with reserved heads; wires excluded. Assembly, retention and magnetic interference need testing.

Readout
TCA9548A + Pico; ADS1115 when nail pads are fitted

designs.title: B2 · One magnetic PCB
designs.status_detail: B2.1 supplies a routed four-layer PCB with clean independent KiCad DRC, checked mounting CAD, a firmware package and raw recorder. No physical B2 has been tested.
designs.summary: Put all five magnetic sensors, the multiplexer and nail ADC on one shaped PCB. Register it with two spacers and a removable backer; retain B1's TPU, magnets and two thin nail pads.
designs.signal: Raw magnetic observations and nail conductance, with a distinct B2 recording identity. Force still requires physical calibration.
designs.best_for: Testing whether one registered board improves assembly and consistency compared with the five-board B1 pilot.
designs.tradeoff: The routing band is wider within the original side profile. Whole-board repair cost, magnetic interference and calibration transfer still need measurement.

TCA9548ARGER multiplexer + ADS1115IDGSR nail ADC

Pico
Raspberry Pi Pico RP2040 running yam-b2/1
At the wrist/base; J1 connects 3V3, GND, SCL/GP5 and SDA/GP4

designs.title: C1 · Differential-strain root force
designs.status_detail: C1.1 supplies nine checked CAD parts, a routed readout PCB with clean independent KiCad DRC, firmware, raw capture and static calibration tools. The bonded-joint structural model passed its numerical checks. No physical C1 has been assembled or tested.
designs.summary: Put eight foil gauges on a transverse metal beam at the finger root. Two bridges measure its bending while the original thin nail and soft TPU keep their contact geometry.
designs.signal: Aggregate normal force after specimen-specific calibration of the two bridges. Raw readings alone are not newtons, and this design has no local contact map.
designs.best_for: Comparing whole-finger force feedback without permanent magnets or sensing film on the leading nail.
designs.tradeoff: Adds 18 mm reach and 21.4 mm to the overall width, making the root 53 mm wide. Reserved hardware extends the back by 24.2 mm. Gauge bonding, clamp slip, thermal drift and moving-arm loads need physical tests.
sensors: A_R1–A_R4
Four Micro-Measurements CEA-13-062UWA-350 foil gauges
Station A: grid centers 8.5 mm from the active beam's fixed boundary; two on top and two underneath
B_R1–B_R4
Four more CEA-13-062UWA-350 gauges
Station B: grid centers 24.5 mm from the same boundary; two on each face
Both stations
350 Ω full bridges; M-Bond 200 initial laboratory bonding process

Readout
Two ADS1232IPWR bridge converters
On the fixed 82 × 64 mm C1 readout PCB near the wrist/base; one four-wire harness per bridge
Health / electrical test
Two INA219AIDR monitors and two TMUX1101DBVR shunt switches
On the readout PCB; excitation checks and startup electrical tests do not verify gauge bonding
Controller
Raspberry Pi Pico RP2040 running yam-c1/1
At the wrist/base; J1 carries clock, data, control and power
designs.placement: Machine the 33 × 22 × 14 mm active beam and its carriers from 6061-T6 aluminum. The floating carrier holds the complete original finger; the fixed carrier attaches to the jaw. All finger loads pass through the beam. The 1.57 × 3.05 mm active grids sit on its top and bottom faces. The original nail and TPU receive no added sensor layers.

designs.title: N1 · Bare nail with strain sensing
designs.status_detail: N1.1 supplies four checked CAD parts, complete material around its fasteners, a converged metal structural screen, combined Pico firmware and physical static-calibration tools. The C1 bridge PCB and R1 TPU interfaces are reused. No physical N1 specimen has been tested.
designs.summary: Use a bare steel fork with two shear-sensing webs behind the nail. Four retained R1 cells cover the compliant TPU, and one Pico records all six sensing signals.
designs.signal: Nail normal force after two-bridge calibration, plus four calibrated TPU force proxies. Contact on fixed structure can bypass these paths; no six-axis or dense contact-map claim.
designs.best_for: Testing thin leading-nail access and normal-force feedback when surface-pad thickness or wear matters.
designs.tradeoff: Three machined steel parts, gauge bonding and a larger side envelope. Body width is about 38.7 mm, or 40 mm with the proposed screw ends. Complete force, pose, contact and durability tests remain.

A separate revised PETG frame clears the webs while retaining the central frame and three TPU attachment regions. Build CH2–CH5 on the original TPU and keep the metal nail bare.

designs.title: B3 · Recessed magnetic board
designs.status_detail: B3.1 supplies five checked CAD solids, the retained B2 PCB, a sampled magnetic-range review, gain-5 firmware and raw capture. Physical assembly, frame stiffness and 20 N qualification remain pending.
designs.summary: Move the magnetic board inward by 2.44 mm using a separately recessed hard frame and tapered locating spacers. Keep the compliant B1 insert, four magnets and two thin nail pads.
designs.signal: Gain-5 magnetic-field observations and two nail conductances. Physical calibration is required to estimate force.
designs.best_for: A paired B2/B3 experiment to determine whether a narrower board assembly helps precision access.
designs.tradeoff: Adds 3.61 mm global width with reserved heads, compared with B2's 6.05 mm; wires excluded. The changed frame, smaller spacer feet, actual deformation and interference require tests.

designs.title: F1 · Dense resistive contact matrix
designs.status_detail: R3 has a checked fanout, twelve routed sensing foils, a 64-location map and matching carrier/fit files. Wrist readout and raw code are available. Finished mating/lamination, the full resistance budget, object/motion clearance and the complete physical finger remain unfinished.
designs.summary: Place a custom pressure-film matrix on each nail prong and each of four TPU contact regions: 64 intended electrical contact locations, with rigid readout electronics at the wrist.
designs.signal: Raw electrical response at a 4 × 16 allocation. Force, contact thresholds and crosstalk behavior require physical calibration.
designs.best_for: Denser contact location when it justifies custom flex manufacture and additional electronics.
designs.tradeoff: Twelve flexible foils, a side fanout and a wrist board add assembly work and volume. Dense coverage does not establish reliable contact or accurate force.

At the wrist/base, connected to the fanout by a 50-conductor cable
designs.placement: The tactile sensor is the film/electrode laminate at the contact surface. Nominal layer-reference additions are 0.455 mm at the nail and 0.72 mm at the TPU. The PCB, ADC and connectors stay off the flexible contact faces. Paper patterns are mechanical fit tools, not routed sensor foils.

designs.title: K1 · Shielded capacitive cells
designs.status_detail: 49 current CAD parts, casting patterns, conforming supports, a checked readout PCB and raw code are supplied. Electrode artwork, retention/stops, venting, cable/enclosure integration and physical qualification remain.
designs.summary: Place compression capacitors on the two nail prongs and four TPU regions, with protected reference cells and fixed readout electronics.
designs.signal: Capacitance changes; force depends on the mechanical dielectric structure and calibration.
designs.best_for: A possible alternative when magnetic interference is unacceptable.
designs.tradeoff: The current stack adds thickness and assembly steps. Plate/post mechanics, creep, parasitics, moisture and bending artifacts need measurement.

designs.title: Pneumatic finger · Internal air channels
designs.status_detail: FORTE is a relevant published reference. No ENPIRE adaptation or 20 N version has been designed here.
designs.summary: Sense deformation of a compliant finger through changes in internal air pressure, with pressure transducers located away from the contact surface.
designs.signal: Pressure measurements interpreted as force/slip through a validated mechanical model.
designs.best_for: A passive soft interface with electronics at the wrist.
designs.tradeoff: Sealing, tubing, temperature/volume effects and the demonstrated force range require attention.

designs.placement: The compliant chamber is the contact element. Tubes connect it to fixed pressure sensors. The published reference reports a 0–8 N experiment; a 20 N ENPIRE design still needs new range and mechanical work.

next_steps: Reproduce a reference pressure chamber before modifying the finger.

designs.best_for: Tasks that need dense contact shape or texture information.
designs.tradeoff: Optical path, lighting, gel fabrication, processing and the thin-nail interface require a substantial redesign.

designs.title: FB1 · Packaged force button at the root
designs.status_detail: FB1.1 supplies 54 CAD parts/references, a checked two-layer PCB, raw Pico acquisition, calibration tools and an independent structural screen. Physical specimens tested: 0.
designs.summary: Mount the complete original finger on four metal leaf guides. A flat adjustable plunger loads one Honeywell FMA sensor at the root, preserving the thin nail and compliant TPU contact surfaces.
designs.signal: Raw coupled sensor load. External finger force requires specimen-specific calibration; no contact-location map is produced.
designs.best_for: Testing a purchased digital force element without a tactile film on the leading nail, and comparing its setup and accuracy with L1 and C1.
designs.tradeoff: Adds 50 mm reach and several clamps. Alignment, preload, cable forces and stop settings need care. The factory error specification does not guarantee the project's 0.5 N force or 0.2 N contact targets.
